_about: Sample GuardEvent bodies, one or more per tenet, each verified to trip the rails it claims. Wired into the Swagger UI at /docs as the named examples on POST /v1/guard and POST /v1/guard/stream, so the API can be driven from the browser without reading the source.
_synthetic: EVERY VALUE HERE IS SYNTHETIC. The SSN and card number are the standard test values; the NPI and DEA are check-digit-valid and fictitious; the AWS key and secret are AWS's own published documentation examples. Nothing in this file is or resembles a live credential, and nothing here should be replaced with one - the file is committed.
_verified: The expect_detectors list on each sample was produced by running the sample through POST /v1/guard and reading back the detectors that fired, not by reading the rail source. tests/test_gateway.py re-asserts it, so a sample that stops tripping its tenet fails the suite rather than sitting in the docs misleading someone.
_fail_closed: Most of these samples BLOCK on a fresh install - not because of the finding, but because Stage-2 rails with no model weights report unjudged, and unjudged fails closed. That is the platform behaving as designed. Read the `findings` array rather than the decision to see what was actually detected; there is deliberately no request field that turns fail-closed off.

samples.name: explainability_malformed_json
samples.summary: Explainability - a structured answer that does not parse (step/response)
samples.why: Two rails answer, by design: the explainability rail says WHY it failed (the decoder's own position message) and the reliability rail says THAT it failed. Different categories, different detectors, one verdict.

samples.name: accountability_attack_replay
samples.summary: Accountability - a replay of a previously confirmed attack
samples.why: NOTE: this fires NOTHING on a fresh install, and that is correct. The mounted rail is a Rebuff-style self-hardening corpus that is EMPTY at import - it only matches once an operator or a CI run has confirmed a first attack. Accountability's real contribution to every request is infrastructure the other samples exercise implicitly: the threshold read, the fail_mode decision, and the audit row written for this very request.
